landing.title: A wargame for Move on Sui
landing.description: Move-over is a Web3/Move-based wargame inspired by Ethernaut and overthewire.org, played on the Sui blockchain. Each level is a smart contract that needs to be 'hacked'. The game is 100% open source and all levels are contributions made by other players. Do you have an interesting idea? PRs are welcome.
landing.subtitle: Browser-based Move security wargame
landing.intro: Move-over is a browser-first CTF for Move security. Read vulnerable contracts, write the `run()` exploit path, and return the right `*Flag` to clear each level.

landing.sectionTitle: Move Smart Contract Security in a Browser Runtime
landing.sectionIntro: Move-over is a browser-based security playground where you learn by doing. Instead of reading theory only, you inspect vulnerable contract code, write an exploit flow, run it instantly, and verify that your solution can return the expected proof object. The core loop is practical: read, write, run, return, and improve.
landing.howItWorksTitle: How the Move-over Browser Workflow Operates
landing.howItWorksBody: Every level runs in an in-browser runtime, so there is no wallet setup, chain state dependency, or local VM requirement to start practicing. You focus on Move security logic: ownership checks, capability misuse, object state transitions, and how to craft a safe, reproducible exploit path that passes verification.
landing.writeRunTitle: Write `run()`, Return the `Flag`, and Pass the Level
landing.writeRunBody: Your target is explicit: write the `run()` body so it can return the correct `*Flag` object for the challenge. If the return type and behavior match the level contract requirements, the level is cleared and your progress is saved.
landing.coreSkill1: Read and reason about Move smart contract security behavior.
landing.coreSkill2: Write exploit-oriented logic in a controlled browser environment.
landing.coreSkill3: Return proof objects correctly and validate deterministic outcomes.
landing.recommendedBody: Start with Genesis for fundamentals, continue with Lockbox for object manipulation patterns, and then tackle Fallout for deeper exploit reasoning. This sequence builds practical Move security intuition step by step.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
howToPlay.welcome: Welcome to a tiny browser-based heist simulator. Each level gives you a vulnerable Move module, and your job is to write `run()` so it returns the glorious `Flag`.
howToPlay.step1: Read the level instructions and inspect the contract code like a detective with too much coffee.
howToPlay.step2: Write only the body of `run()` in the editor.
howToPlay.step3: Capture the `Flag` and return it from `run()`; no `Flag`, no victory.
howToPlay.step4: Click Run, watch the verifier judge your life choices, then iterate and move to the next level.
